subject: Next steps: Offline handoff & HW clarifications for Genomex on-prem eval
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Porter <michael.porter@genomex.co>, Ops Team <ops@genomex.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: Offline handoff & HW clarifications for Genomex on-prem eval

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion and appreciate the clarity on your constraints. Short recap + concrete asks so we can keep momentum on the on-prem / air-gapped evaluation: 

What we heard from Genomex on the call:
- Primary preference: private on-prem appliance (air-gapped) for IP/data control. Hosted API and Dedicated capacity were reviewed but ruled out for this workload due to regulatory constraints.
- Ops constraint: limited maintenance windows (overnight weekday windows only), prefers minimal onsite interventions.
- Patching preference: would like offline/physical patch process (vendored media or USB) unless we can certify signed offline bundles.
- HSM/KMS: you have an internal HSM; want to know how Redwood integrates with customer KMS/HSM in an air-gapped setup.
- Spares & swap support: need clarity on which components are user-serviceable versus Redwood-managed (GPU modules, NVMe, PSU).

Open items / asks (actionable):
1) Please complete the attached rack & power template and return by EOD Friday 2026-11-13 so we can validate power/cooling and rack unit needs. (attachment: rack_and_power_template.xlsx)
2) Confirm outbound allowances for the appliance: list of allowed egress domains/ports or whether completely blocked. If blocked, confirm procedure for signed patch media.
3) Confirm if Genomex can accept quarterly offline patch windows (we proposed a 2–4 hour window) or if your schedule requires longer intervals (e.g., 6 months).
4) Share the primary contact for physical site coordination (onsite ops) + shipping address for hardware spares and acceptance testing.
5) Provide any company-specific compliance artifacts we should review early (e.g., on-prem SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration docs).

Attachments: redwood_offline_handoff_checklist_v1.pdf (checklist of runbook items we need), rack_and_power_template.xlsx

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Ben Carter (cc): will coordinate site-survey scheduling and logistics.
- Priyom Das (cc): will lead technical runbook exchange (MOPs, rollback steps) and follow up on kernel/driver/firmware compatibility.
- Stephanie (me): will coordinate HSM/KMS engineering intro and draft the mutual action plan.

Target timeline:
- Genomex returns rack/power template & egress confirmation by 2026-11-13.
- Redwood to propose site-survey dates for week of 2026-11-16.

If anything above is incorrect, please flag. Otherwise, we’ll proceed on the timeline above.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Michael Porter <michael.porter@genomex.co>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@genomex.co>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: Offline handoff & HW clarifications for Genomex on-prem eval

Thanks, Stephanie — helpful recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Patch cadence: our preference is 6-month offline windows, but we can accommodate a shorter window for critical security patches if you recommend it. Quarterly would be difficult operationally.
- HSM/KMS: we run an on-prem HSM (Thales) and cannot expose network calls to an external KMS. We need details on the integration model (e.g., do you ship a PKCS#11-compatible agent that runs locally?). Also, we need to confirm that private keys never leave our HSM.
- Spares: our ops team prefers to swap NVMe/PSU but not GPU modules. Swapping GPUs requires a forklift/low-level firmware handoff that we typically avoid. Can Redwood confirm which components must be RMA'd vs can be user-swapped?
- Outbound: currently all outbound is blocked by default; we have a change window for opening egress for the device for registration/orchestration if absolutely necessary. Otherwise we need an offline registration option.

Action items on our side:
- I’ll get the rack/power template back to you by Friday (2026-11-13).
- Lauren Chen (cc) is our ops lead — she’ll provide the onsite contact and physical address by EOD Thursday.
- We’ll attach our HSM integration guidance (high level) — we can’t share nitty-gritty keys yet but will share the integration requirements.

On the GPU swap question — we are also interested in a physical maintenance SLA: what response time do you guarantee for RMA and onsite replacement in the US West region?

Thanks,
Michael
Director, Platform Ops | Genomex Labs
michael.porter@genomex.co | +1 (206) 555-0241

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Porter <michael.porter@genomex.co>, Lauren Chen <lauren.chen@genomex.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: Offline handoff & HW clarifications for Genomex on-prem eval

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 4:30 PM Michael Porter <michael.porter@genomex.co> wrote:
> Thanks, Stephanie — helpful recap. A few clarifications from my side: 
> 
> - Patch cadence: our preference is 6-month offline windows...
> - HSM/KMS: we run an on-prem HSM (Thales)...
> - Spares: our ops team prefers to swap NVMe/PSU but not GPU modules...
> - Outbound: currently all outbound is blocked by default...

Thanks for the quick clarifications — this is all actionable and expected. Quick notes and who will follow up: 

1) Patching cadence: noted — 6-month regular windows OK. Priyom, can you confirm whether we can compress critical security updates into emergency signed offline bundles and what the verification/signing workflow would look like? (Priyom: owning)
2) HSM/KMS: Redwood can run a PKCS#11-compatible agent that communicates only with the local HSM. Keys do not leave the HSM; we can provide a security architecture doc and schedule a short call between your HSM admin and our security engineer. (Stephanie: I’ll set up the intro this week.)
3) Spares / RMA: Ben — can you confirm Redwood’s maintenance SLA options for US-West (onsite RMA response times and whether GPU swaps require Redwood field engineers)? We’ll capture exact RMA timelines in the mutual action plan.
4) Outbound/registration: We have an offline registration option that uses signed device manifests exchanged over your secure channel. Ben, I’ll need you to confirm the exact process and provide the manifest template.

Next steps & immediate owners: 
- Priyom Das: draft MOP for offline patch signing & verification, and list of required runbook items (target: 2026-11-17).
- Ben Carter: confirm maintenance SLA options & RMA routing for GPUs/PSUs (target: 2026-11-15).
- Stephanie Nguyen: schedule HSM/ security architecture intro with Genomex HSM admin and Redwood security engineer (target: 2026-11-12).
- Genomex: return rack/power template & egress confirmation by 2026-11-13.

I’ve attached the current handoff checklist and rack template again. If any of the timelines above are too aggressive for your ops calendar, flag which items to extend and we’ll reprioritize.

Thanks all — will follow up with calendar invites.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172
